notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET — NOT RECORDABLE (agent_supports: no; daemon_capability: n/a; driver_capability: n/a). This spec states the arc the row asserts so a future re-assessment has something concrete to compare against; it is NOT expected to pass on pi 0.83.0 and is deliberately not weakened to match what pi can do. THE ROW: two DISTINCT waiting episodes in one session — one raised by a MUTATING tool, one raised by a READ-ONLY tool — with the arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready and a final ready that survives a >=10s trailing idle. WHY IT CANNOT PASS (agent layer, not transport): pi 0.83.0 ships no per-call permission gate for EITHER tool class. README.md:499 'No permission popups'; docs/usage.md:296 'intentionally does not include ... permission popups'; docs/security.md:31 'No Built-in Sandbox' — built-in tools run with the pi process's permissions, so nothing blocks before a tool runs. A grep over the 180 non-vendor dist/*.js files finds no approval machinery at all: /permission/i returns only an MIT licence header and a clipboard-error comment, and the single ui.select( call site in the whole bundle is core/project-trust.js:9, a startup dialog that belongs to no tool call (scenario 2.27's subject). pi's tool CLASSES do exist — built-ins are read, bash, edit, write, grep, find, ls (docs/usage.md:214) — so the distinction this row draws is expressible for pi; only the dialog is missing. THE PHASE ORDER BELOW (read-only gate then mutating gate) is arbitrary: the row asserts only that each class produces its own episode, not their order. TWO-TOOL CONSTRAINT: this schema carries no tool-name field, so a recipe driving both gates through pi's single `bash` tool would satisfy every phase below while proving nothing about tool class — a re-record must read the transcript's own tool_use blocks and confirm two DISTINCT tool names (read/grep for the read-only half, write/edit for the mutating half). FALSE-POSITIVE WARNING for the mutating half: SignalOpenToolStalled (core/domain/session/signal_hold.go; isPermissionGatedEditTool in metrics.go:503-545 names pi's lowercase write/edit explicitly) flips an open edit-class tool to waiting after stalledEditToolThreshold=30s with no dialog anywhere — so a green mutating_gate_waiting is not by itself evidence of a permission gate, and that fallback is armed for edit-class tools ONLY, never for read/grep/find/ls, so it can never manufacture the read-only half.

text: The single prompt starts the turn → working
The READ-ONLY tool's permission dialog opens → its own waiting episode, entered while the dialog is on screen
User answers the read-only dialog → back to working
The MUTATING tool's permission dialog opens → a SECOND, distinct waiting episode (not merged with the first)
User answers the mutating dialog → back to working
Session stays ready across a >=10s trailing idle — it does not fall back to waiting after the last dialog closes
Driver tears the REPL down → process_exited on the session
